name: Ready-made metadata: Google METADATA.pb, Google site metadata (fonts.google.com/metadata/fonts) and font-file tables (OS/2, PANOSE, post)
what_it_is: Three free sources of structural facts, none of them mood. (1) METADATA.pb, one file per Google family in google/fonts: name, designer, license, category (SANS_SERIF, DISPLAY, ...), date_added, subsets, axes, and for some families stroke and classifications. Checked on two families: Orbitron has stroke SANS_SERIF and classifications DISPLAY; Exo 2 has neither. (2) The unofficial https://fonts.google.com/metadata/fonts JSON (the app already fetches it): 1,950 families with category, stroke (Sans Serif, Serif, Slab Serif), classifications (Display, Handwriting, Monospace, Symbols), popularity and trending ranks, dateAdded, designers, axes, and per style key ('400', '400i') the legacy 1-10 values thickness, slant and width plus lineHeight. (3) Tables inside every font file: OS/2 usWeightClass, usWidthClass and PANOSE (10 numbers), post.italicAngle and isFixedPitch, which fontkit reads without extra work.
provider_and_url: Google Fonts: https://github.com/google/fonts (e.g. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/fonts/main/ofl/orbitron/METADATA.pb); https://fonts.google.com/metadata/fonts (undocumented; the app uses it as GF_METADATA_URL in server/catalog.ts, line 10, and strips an anti-XSSI prefix). The font tables are part of the OpenType files themselves (OS/2 and post tables), published by each font's designer.
catalog_coverage: Measured by me from /tmp/gfmeta.json and the app's rebuilt merged catalog (2,099 rows). SITE METADATA (category, stroke, classifications, popularity, dateAdded, axes): 1,621 of 1,760 Google-source rows (92.1%); the 139 missing are 115 non-Google Fontsource families plus 24 true Google families (new or renamed). Fontshare 0/64, Velvetyne 0/63, Collletttivo 0/26, Tunera 0/23, Use & Modify 0/163: nothing for the 339 non-Google-source rows. Within the 1,621: stroke present 1,143 (70.5%), classifications non-empty 975 (60.2%), popularity 1,621 (100%). Google's category equals the Fontsource-derived category on all 1,621 rows, so it adds no information. LEGACY 1-10 thickness/slant/width: 714 of 1,950 site families (claim confirmed) and 711 of the 1,760 catalog Google rows (40.4%). They exist only for families added 2010-2016 (710 of the 714; the other four are dated 2017, 2020 and 2026), so they are frozen and will never cover new families. FONT TABLES: readable in 100% of files I opened. Indie: all 275 cached upright files (Velvetyne 63, Collletttivo 26, Tunera 23, Use & Modify 163). Fontshare: 64 of 64 (one regular file per family, fetched by me from cdn.fontshare.com, 1.7 MB). Google: a random sample of 60 Fontsource latin-400 woff2 files from jsDelivr (1.5 MB), not all 1,644, so Google percentages carry sampling error.
granularity: Site metadata: family level for category/stroke/classifications/popularity; per style for the legacy values ('400' and '400i' each have their own thickness, slant, width); axes listed per variable family (in the 411 variable catalog families: wght 394, wdth 60, opsz 29, slnt 23). Font tables: per file, so per style; italicAngle shows up in the italic or slanted file, and a variable file gives one value for the default instance only.
signal_type: Overall visual look and geometry (weight, width, slant, serif or sans, monospace, display vs handwriting) plus popularity. No semantic mood.
mood_dimensions_covered: MOTION/ACTIVE (partial, via slant): legacy slant (mean over upright styles) correlates r=0.51 with Google's Active tag (Pearson; Spearman 0.42; n=712) and r=0.53 outside handwriting (n=590), but only 104 of 710 families have any slant above 1 (64 handwriting, 36 display), so it marks scripts and a few display faces. In the files, italicAngle is non-zero in only 4 of 275 upright indie files (Feroniapi -16, Azabache -10, 3270 -5, Vintage Propagandist -1) and 5 of 64 Fontshare files (Kihim -34, Britney -24, Sharpie -19, Kola -10, Comico +5); slanted designs mostly live in separate italic files (65 of the 275 indie winners have italicFiles). Kihim's designer text says every letter is 'set on an extreme angle'; italicAngle -34 says it without any text. LOUD: legacy thickness (mean over styles) r=0.73 with Loud (n=714; the outline claimed 0.77; max over styles gives 0.57). Same signal as quant.csv stroke width (r=0.83 over 1,394 families), so the 1-10 value is redundant. FUTURISTIC/TECHNO: nothing tracks it. Legacy width vs Futuristic r=0.10, vs Techno 0.10; slant -0.09 and -0.05; thickness 0.04 (n=714). CALM/ELEGANT/HANDMADE/PLAYFUL: not expressible (thickness vs Calm r=-0.05). Handmade is only the coarse category 'handwriting' or classification 'Handwriting'. WIDTH (condensed, wide): usWidthClass is off the default 5 in 31 of 275 indie files (11%; Aujournuit Wide 9, Sprat Extended 9, Halibut Condensed 3) but in 0 of 64 Fontshare files (Gambarino is a condensed serif and says 5) and 2 of 60 Google files. MONOSPACE: isFixedPitch true in 10 of 275 indie, 3 of 60 Google, 0 of 64 Fontshare; the category field already covers this. SERIF/CONTRAST: PANOSE would give serif style and contrast but is empty (see untagged_rows).
query_style_specificity: Helps only blunt structural requests ('heavy', 'condensed', 'wide', 'monospace', 'slanted') and does nothing for mood words such as techno, friendly, elegant or fast. For 'fast movement' it contributes slant at best.
quality_evidence: Measured offline by me; no LLM test. Correlations with Google's human tags (families with legacy values, tags missing counted as 0): thickness mean vs Loud 0.73, slant (upright mean) vs Active 0.51 and Excited 0.33, width vs Futuristic 0.10, vs Loud 0.23. Using quant.csv instead of the legacy thickness lifts the Loud correlation to 0.83 and covers 1,394 families, not 714. The font tables are weak: usWidthClass sits at the default 5 in 244 of 275 indie files (89%) and in all 64 Fontshare files (I did not judge usWeightClass: I opened one regular file per family, so a rate would be circular). The app's own collletttivo.ts says 'Both Demi and Regular carry usWeightClass 400' and usemodify.ts notes Tuffy's Regular says 500, which is why those builders already correct weights by name. PANOSE is mostly empty (below). No published test of these fields for mood retrieval found.
known_noise: Table values: usWeightClass 1 in Kikuta (invalid; the app's clampWeight guards this), Fontshare weights 375, 378 and 421 in three files, default-filled width classes (above), PANOSE all zeros in 113 of 275 indie files (41%), 32 of 60 Google files (53%) and 63 of 64 Fontshare files (98%); where PANOSE is filled, the contrast field is non-zero in only 42 of 275 indie files (15%), 8 of 60 Google files (13%) and 0 of 64 Fontshare files. Legacy values: frozen since 2016; slant is 1 (upright) for 1,018 of 1,378 style entries, so the scale is compressed. Site endpoint: unofficial, can change shape without notice. 'stroke' is null for 29.5% of the catalog's Google rows.
name_and_memory_bias: Numbers carry no names, so a ranking built on them does not depend on evocative names. But the model would only see numbers or buckets, and has to translate its memory of 'Orbitron' into 'wide, heavy', so name and memory bias moves into the translation step. Popularity (already used: rank <= 150 marks 'very common') is the one bias-related field here and is already exploited.
untagged_rows: Silently dropped if used to rank: legacy values are missing for 59.6% of Google rows and 100% of indie and Fontshare rows; site metadata is missing for all 339 non-Google-source rows. The font tables exist for every row but the width class and PANOSE are mostly default-filled, so a 'condensed' filter built on usWidthClass would miss most condensed indie and all Fontshare fonts, and a PANOSE filter would miss 41% (indie), 53% (Google sample) and 98% (Fontshare). Missing values must be treated as unknown, never as 'average'.
text_interference_risk: Not applicable: numbers, nothing is rendered.
integration_path: ALREADY IN THE APP: popularity (rank, 'very common' <= 150, date added) and the stroke field only to add a 'Slab' tag (server/catalog.ts); usWeightClass is read in server/sources/*.ts only to pick weights and italics. NOT READ: usWidthClass, PANOSE, italicAngle, isFixedPitch (src/facts/core.ts reads cap height, x-height, ascender, descender, overshoot, kerning, features and axes only), classifications, and the legacy 1-10 values. OPTION A (extra catalog fields): at build time, in the same pass that already opens each file (server/sources/common.ts readFontInfo, and src/facts for Google/Fontshare), add italicAngle, usWidthClass, isFixedPitch and write them with the other catalog fields; print coarse tokens in compactCatalog only when informative, e.g. `... | slanted 24deg, wide, mono`. OPTION B (precomputed file): server/data/traits.json = {"Kihim": {"slant": -34, "width": 5, "fixed": false, "stroke400": 61}} keyed by family, merged at catalog build. OPTION C (a score step): not worth it for these fields alone; fold them into the measured-traits item's own feature vector. Take Google's classifications and popularity at no cost; skip the legacy 1-10 values and PANOSE.
tokens_per_row: Plus 2-5 tokens per row where a bucket applies (about 4-10k tokens if every row got one; only about 15-20% of rows would carry a non-default width, slant or mono token, so about 2-3k tokens in practice). Static between searches, so the prompt stays cacheable.
vocabulary_alignment: Adds new terms (condensed, wide, slanted, monospace, heavy) that are plain design words, not Google's mood tags. They do not map onto Google's Expressive vocabulary, except weakly: heavy -> Loud and slant -> Active.
explainability: Yes, strongly: 'slanted 24 degrees' or 'stroke 61/1000' is a measured value a person can verify, which is the best explanation any item in this set offers, though only for shape words.
determinism: Fully deterministic data. The final picks stay as variable as today's Haiku call unless a scoring step is added.
build_effort: Small: about half a day to read the extra tables (fontkit is already a dependency and each builder already opens the files), about 2 hours to add Google's classifications, plus tests and a regression check on the catalog rules version. An agent can do it in this codebase; the work I did here (reading 399 files in under a minute) is the proof of concept.
per_search_cost_and_latency: None added per search beyond +2-3k cached prompt tokens; no extra call.
one_off_cost: Indie files are already cached (275 files). Fontshare: 64 files, 1.7 MB (done by me once). Google: about 25 KB per latin woff2 (60 files = 1.5 MB), so all 1,644 families would be ~40 MB from jsDelivr, once; or use facts the app already computes.
human_effort: About 1 hour to choose bucket thresholds (what counts as 'wide' or 'slanted') and look at 20 results. None as the catalog grows.
asset_access: Open. Site metadata: one request to fonts.google.com/metadata/fonts per catalog rebuild (already done). METADATA.pb is not needed because the site JSON already carries the same fields (1,700 raw.githubusercontent requests would only repeat it). Font files: indie via the app's own cache and proxy (hosts gitlab.com, codeberg.org, usemodify.com...), Fontsource via cdn.jsdelivr.net, Fontshare via cdn.fontshare.com (URL is the API `file` value plus '.woff2'; 404 without the suffix).
licence_and_provenance: Site endpoint: undocumented and unofficial, no stated terms [uncertain], already relied on by the app. METADATA.pb and google/fonts: no root LICENSE; README says top-level directories indicate the licence of files inside [uncertain for metadata files]. Table values are facts about the files; storing a few numbers per family is not redistributing font software, so the licence of the fonts (OFL, Apache, Ubuntu UFL; Fontshare ITF Free Font License; indie OFL or similar) is not engaged [uncertain, not legal advice]. This item makes no derived images.
etiquette: Never touch velvetyne.fr: the cached Velvetyne files I read came from the app's existing cache (GitLab), I requested nothing from Velvetyne. My own requests: 60 jsDelivr files and 64 Fontshare CDN files, 0.4-0.5 s apart, with a descriptive User-Agent, one pass; two raw.githubusercontent METADATA.pb checks; no robots or bot-protection issue met (one mistake: 64 requests with a wrong URL returned 404 before I added the .woff2 suffix, nothing blocked).
maintenance_and_freshness: Site metadata is live (popularity and trending move, new families appear with dateAdded). Legacy 1-10 values are frozen (4 families added after 2016). Font tables are as current as the files. Work to keep current: the catalog build already refetches the site JSON; new indie or Fontshare files need one table read each.
risks_and_limitations: (1) None of this expresses mood, and nothing here tracks Futuristic or Techno. (2) Default-filled tables look like data: 'width 5' says 'normal' for Gambarino, a condensed face. (3) The legacy values cover 40% of Google rows and no new families. (4) Slant describes scripts and a few display faces, not 'fast' type in general; Exo 2 and Saira italics are separate files. (5) Variable files report only the default instance. (6) The site endpoint is unofficial. (7) Google sample is 60 files; Google percentages could be off by roughly 10 points. (8) Google's category matches Fontsource's on all rows, so it should not be mistaken for new signal.
evaluation_hook: Predict Google's Active, Loud and Condensed-like tags from the new fields on held-out families (done in part: Loud 0.83 with stroke width, Active 0.51 with slant); then show rated result grids for 'heavy', 'condensed' and 'slanted' queries before and after, which should improve clearly for those words only.
recommendation_for_font_explorer: USE PARTLY, and keep expectations low: this is bookkeeping, not vibe. Keep popularity (already used). Add Google classifications and read italicAngle, usWidthClass and isFixedPitch as free by-products where the app already opens the file, to give the model plain shape words (slanted, wide, condensed, mono). Skip the legacy 1-10 values (frozen, 40% coverage, redundant with quant stroke width) and skip PANOSE (41% to 98% empty). Do not pay for anything that tries to read mood from these. Relative to the other items: it is a subset of the measured-traits item (which should compute slant, width and weight from outlines for all 2,099 rows instead of trusting tables that are default-filled), and it does not help the indie gap beyond slant and width. SMALLEST FIRST STEP: write one script that reads italicAngle, usWidthClass, isFixedPitch and stroke width from the 275 cached indie files and the 64 Fontshare files into a traits file, compare against Google's tags on the Google sample, and only then decide whether the prompt gets the extra words. About half a day.
